newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks marginally higher in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks marginally higher in quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. blue chip and technology stocks drifted at mildly higher levels on Friday morning, helped by solid earnings reports in quiet trade.
The Dow Jones Industrial average, which rebounded from a dose of profit-taking late yesterday, tacked on about 16 points, or 0.20 percent, at 8133.
The Nasdaq composite was up around four points to 1573.
The long bond was up 6/32 to yield 6.43 percent, after digesting June durable goods and existing home sales data.
"The market looks tired here," Chris Dickerson, an analyst at Global Market Strategists, said.
Market breadth was positive, with advancing issues outnumbering decliners on the New York Stock Exchange by 13 to 11. On Nasdaq, advancers barely outpaced declining stocks.
"It's pretty quiet," Jay Meagrow, an institutional trader at McDonald & Co, said. "It looks like a summer Friday. We have had some interesting last half-hours recently, but for now it looks quiet."
Durable goods orders rose 2.3 percent in June. Existing home sales fell 2.6 percent to a 4.14 million annual rate.
